text:
Seiner Hochfürstliche Durchlaucht
Die Gräfin Schlabrendorff wird mit die 50000 rtl. bis Weinachten
oder eigentlich bis den 1ten Januar 1805 warten, zu einen längern
Termin hat sie Homuth nicht bewegen können.
Sie hat sehr kläglich gethan daß sie so viel verliere müste, und
Da sie keine Intressen von dieses Capital erhielte, so wäre der
Verlust noch größer wann sie länger als bis den 1 ten Januar
1805 warten solte —
Ist dem so daß Ewr Durchlaucht bis dahin keine Intressen zahlen
dürfen, so glaube ich daß es leicht fallen wird, sich bey diesen
Termin zu beruhigen. Es sind doch dabey 2500 Rthl gewonnen
und bis zu der Zeit wird Geld genug eingehen —
Homuth bittet um den Vergleich, damit er das nötige auf
sezzen und der Gräfin zur Vollziehung zu schicken könne.
Er wird probiren, ob er bey der Gelegenheit die alten Wechsel
heraus bekommen kan.
Der Conducteur Cabanis ist abgegangen
Er wird sich draußen eine Bauer Fuhre
miethen die er glaubt vor 4 oder 5 rt.
zu erhalten. Hier wolte die Mieths
Kutscher 20 rt. habe und verlangten
noch auf Entter und Gott weis was
eine Beihülfe
Breslau den 29ten Marz 1804.
v Triebenfeld

translation.en:
To His Most Serene Highness. The Countess Schlabrendorff will wait for the 50,000 Rthl. until Christmas, or properly speaking until the 1st of January 1805; to a longer term Homuth has not been able to move her. She made a most piteous business of having to lose so much, and, since she received no interest from this capital, the loss would be greater still were she to wait beyond the 1st of January 1805 — If it be so that Your Serene Highness need pay no interest until that date, then I believe it will come easily to rest content with this term. There are, after all, 2,500 Rthl gained thereby, and by that time money enough will come in — Homuth asks for the settlement, so that he may draw up what is needful and send it to the Countess for execution. He will try whether he can, on that occasion, get the old bills of exchange back.

The surveyor Cabanis has departed. He will hire himself a peasant cart out in the country, which he believes he can get for 4 or 5 Rthl. Here the hackney coachmen wanted to have 20 Rthl. and demanded besides an allowance for [uncertain: Entter] and God knows what else.

Wrocław, the 29th of March 1804.

v Triebenfeld

text_english:
To His Most Serene Highness. The Countess Schlabrendorff will wait for the 50,000 Rthl. until Christmas, or properly speaking until the 1st of January 1805; to a longer term Homuth has not been able to move her. She made a most piteous business of having to lose so much, and, since she received no interest from this capital, the loss would be greater still were she to wait beyond the 1st of January 1805 — If it be so that Your Serene Highness need pay no interest until that date, then I believe it will come easily to rest content with this term. There are, after all, 2,500 Rthl gained thereby, and by that time money enough will come in — Homuth asks for the settlement, so that he may draw up what is needful and send it to the Countess for execution. He will try whether he can, on that occasion, get the old bills of exchange back.

The surveyor Cabanis has departed. He will hire himself a peasant cart out in the country, which he believes he can get for 4 or 5 Rthl. Here the hackney coachmen wanted to have 20 Rthl. and demanded besides an allowance for [uncertain: Entter] and God knows what else.

Wrocław, the 29th of March 1804.

v Triebenfeld
summary_en: Countess Schlabrendorff is willing to wait for the 50,000 Rthl until 1 January 1805. Homuth could not obtain a longer term, and she complains of her loss. If the Prince need pay no interest until then, Triebenfeld advises accepting the date, since 2,500 Rthl would be gained. Homuth asks for the settlement so that he can draw up the deed, and intends to try to get the old bills of exchange back. The surveyor Cabanis has departed and means to hire a peasant's cart outside, which he thinks he can get for 4 or 5 Rthl.
summary_de: Gräfin Schlabrendorff will mit den 50000 Rthl bis zum 1. Januar 1805 warten. Einen längeren Termin konnte Homuth nicht erreichen, sie beklagt ihren Verlust. Muss der Fürst bis dahin keine Zinsen zahlen, rät Triebenfeld, den Termin anzunehmen, da 2500 Rthl gewonnen seien. Homuth bittet um den Vergleich, um die Urkunde aufzusetzen, und will versuchen, die alten Wechsel zurückzubekommen. Der Conducteur Cabanis ist abgereist und will draußen eine Bauernfuhre mieten, die er für 4 oder 5 Rthl zu bekommen glaubt.

reading.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Breslau to the Prince. Gräfin Schlabrendorff will wait for the 50000 Rthl until 1 January 1805. Homuth could not get her to agree to a longer term. If no interest is due before then, Triebenfeld advises accepting, since 2500 Rthl are gained. Homuth asks for the Vergleich so he can draft the deed for the countess, and he will try to get the old Wechsel back. The postscript says Conducteur Cabanis has left and will hire a peasant cart outside the city for 4 or 5 rt. Coachmen in Breslau wanted 20 rt. Nothing here on Trąbczyn. A parallel copy (118b) supports two corrections.
